nodes.name: Wet Chemical Displacement on NF
nodes.procedure: The Ru - LC - Ni(OH)_2 catalyst is synthesized on nickel foam (NF) using a wet chemical displacement strategy. Specifically, the spontaneous redox reaction between Ru^{3+} and Ni accelerates the corrosion of the metal matrix due to the favorable thermodynamic process and the assistance of soluble Cl^-. Meanwhile, Ni^{2+} ions coordinate with OH^- to form low-crystalline nickel hydroxide (LC - Ni(OH)_2). As a result, Ru single atoms are uniformly dispersed on LC - Ni(OH)_2 to obtain Ru - LC - Ni(OH)_2 nanosheet catalyst.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ru single-atom catalyst supported on high-crystalline nickel hydroxide support (Ru - HC - Ni(OH)_2) is prepared by hydrothermal method.
nodes.source_text: Ru single-atom catalyst supported on high-crystalline nickel hydroxide support (Ru - HC - Ni(OH)_2) is prepared by hydrothermal method (Figure 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ exhibits highly open 3D network structure; Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ shown for comparison (Figure 1b,d).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscope SEM) image in Figure 1b indicates that Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ exhibits a highly open 3D network structure compared to Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shows random distribution of order and disorder with lattice fringes of 0.270 nm corresponding to (100) plane of Ni(OH)₂; Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ shows high-quality lattice fringes of (100) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Remarkably, the lattice fringes present a random distribution of order and disorder in the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ (Figure 1c)... the interplanar distance of 0.270 nm corresponds to the (100) crystal plane of Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bright atomic columns identified as isolated Ru single atoms on low crystalline support in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ without Ru nanoparticles; Ru atoms regularly located at Ni sites in Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bright atomic columns isolated on the low crystalline support can be distinguished as Ru single atoms in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂, without the obvious appearance of Ru nanoparticles (Figure 1f and 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru, Ni, and O elements uniformly dispersed in both catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis, Ru, Ni, and O elements are uniformly dispersed in the catalyst (Figure S3 and Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂: Ni 2p shifts to higher BE, Ru 3p peaks at 461.62 eV (3p3/2) and 481.74 eV (3p1/2) show negative shift vs Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂; O 1s oxygen vacancy peak at 531.38 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is noticeable that the Ni 2p binding energy of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shifts to a higher value than that of Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂. On the contrary, the Ru 3p peak of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ exhibits a negative shift... the significant oxygen vacancy peak at 531.38 eV in the O 1s spectrum.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shifts positive vs Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ with higher white line; Ru K-edge: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ lower oxidation state near Ru foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the normalized X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), the Ni K-edge spectra of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shift to positive energy relative to Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂... In Ru K-edge XANES, the oxidation state of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ is lower than that of Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ and close to that of Ru foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shows Ni-O coordination number 5.3 vs 5.9 in Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂; shorter Ru-Ni bond length in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂; no Ru-Ru bond confirms single-atom nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fitting results of Ni K-edge EXAFS show that the coordination number of Ni-O decreases from 5.9 (Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂) to 5.3 (Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂) (Figure S8 and Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shows strong signal indicating unsaturated coordination of metallic Ni sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The strong signal peak of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ also indicates the unsaturated coordination of metallic Ni sites in electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-H* intermediate at 1901 cm⁻¹ stronger in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂; H₃O⁺ signal at 1750 cm⁻¹ only in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂; HBWn peak at 3000 cm⁻¹ increases with voltage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the application of voltage, the formation of Ru-H* intermediate can be observed at 1901 cm⁻¹ for Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ and Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ catalysts... a significant hydronium (H₃O⁺) signal can be detected at 1750 cm⁻¹ in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shows H₃O⁺ O-H bending at 3525 cm⁻¹ increasing with potential, absent in Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4e, an obvious absorption band is observed for Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ at the vibration frequency of 3525 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the bending of the O-H groups in H₃O⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: Both catalysts consistent with (100) crystal plane of Ni(OH)₂ (JCPDS 73-1520) (Figure S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1e, the high-quality lattice fringes in Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ are also assigned to the (100) crystal plane, consistent with the X-ray diffraction (XRD) results (Figure S1).
